transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess... what finally got me here is that I can't seem to keep my focus on one thing at work anymore. I'm an electrician, you know? And lately, I sit down to do an estimate or fill out a code form, and... well, someone drops a wrench across the room, or my phone buzzes with a text, or I suddenly get this brilliant idea about how to reorganize the whole workshop. Next thing I know, I'm completely off track. 

Actually, speaking of the workshop, I was thinking about building these custom racks for the conduit. You know how the PVC always rolls around in the back of the van? It drives me crazy. I saw this guy on YouTube who used old pallets to make a sliding drawer system, and I thought, I could totally do that, but better. I even started drawing up plans on the back of a work order the other day. 

But yeah, anyway, the problem is that jobs are starting to get mixed up because I can't finish one thought before another one takes over. My boss is getting pretty annoyed.
Are you having trouble focusing or getting distracted at home or in your free time, not just at work?

At home? Um... I haven't really noticed, to be honest. I don't think so? I mean, usually when I get off work, I just head straight out to the garage anyway. I've been trying to fix up this old dirt bike. It's a '98 Yamaha, two-stroke. Man, those older engines are just built different, you know? You don't see that kind of simplicity anymore. 

Actually, I was looking for a replacement carburetor online the other night, and I ended up going down this massive rabbit hole about how they used to machine the parts back in the nineties. There's this whole forum dedicated to it, and this one guy in Ohio was selling a vintage exhaust pipe, but he wanted way too much for shipping. Shipping costs are just completely out of control lately. Like, I tried to mail a package to my sister for her birthday last month, just a small box, and they wanted thirty bucks! Can you believe that? She lives in Texas, but still. Texas is huge, though. I drove through there once on a road trip a few years ago and it took like two whole days just to get across it... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my free time. Yeah, I don't know, I guess I just do stuff around the house.
Did you have trouble paying attention or getting easily distracted when you were a kid?

As a kid? Um, no, I don't think I had any problems like that back then. I actually liked school alright, especially whenever we got to do hands-on stuff. Like, I remember in eighth grade we had this science fair, and I built this electromagnet out of a giant iron nail and some copper wire. I stripped the wire myself. My dad got it from his buddy who worked at the scrap yard. 

Man, that scrap yard was insane, just mountains of metal everywhere. We used to go down there on Saturdays and look for old car parts. Dad was always trying to restore this '68 Mustang, but he could never find the right alternator bracket. People charge an arm and a leg for classic car parts now. It's like, just because it's old doesn't mean it's made of gold, right? I mean, half the time it's rusted through anyway. You gotta soak it in white vinegar for like a week just to get the bolts loose. Vinegar is actually crazy useful, though. I use it to clean the coffee maker at the shop all the time because the hard water buildup gets so bad. The guys never clean it, they just keep making coffee over the old grounds, which is disgusting... 

Wait. Sorry. What did you ask me about being a kid?
Do you find yourself getting distracted or having trouble focusing when you're doing something you enjoy, like working on your dirt bike?

Um, no, not really. If it's something I actually want to do, like working on the Yamaha, I can stay locked in for hours. I was actually out in the garage until like 2 AM last night just trying to get the spark plug gapped perfectly. You have to be super precise with it, otherwise it just won't fire right. 

I have this specialized tool for it, actually. It's like a little metal coin with tapered edges. My grandpa gave it to me years ago. He used to be an aviation mechanic, worked on crop dusters out in the Midwest. Man, crop dusting seems like a wild job, just flying super low to the ground all day. I bet the insurance on those planes is absolutely ridiculous. 

Speaking of insurance, my auto rates just went up again for literally no reason. I haven't even had a ticket in five years! The whole system is just a massive scam, honestly. They get you coming and going. Like, you're required by law to have it, so they can just charge whatever they want, and if you complain, they just tell you it's a state-wide adjustment. State-wide, right. It's just greed. I was telling my buddy Mike about it, and he said... wait. Sorry. What did you ask me? Something about the dirt bike? Yeah, no, I don't get distracted with that stuff at all.
Do you find that you get more distracted when you're feeling stressed or anxious?

Stressed? Um... I don't really know. I don't feel like I get that stressed out, honestly. I mean, my job can be pretty demanding, being an electrician and all. You definitely have to be on your toes when you're dealing with live wires. One wrong move and you're getting a serious shock. 

I actually got zapped pretty good a couple of years ago when I was working on a commercial job downtown. They were renovating this old bank building into luxury apartments. It's crazy what they're doing with some of these old buildings now. They just gut the whole thing and leave the brick exposed, throw in some stainless steel appliances, and suddenly they're charging three grand a month for a studio. Who can even afford that? It's mostly tech people moving here, I guess. 

They opened up this new artisanal donut shop on the ground floor of that building. The donuts are like six bucks each. Six bucks! And they put weird stuff on them, like bacon and maple syrup, or lavender. I tried the lavender one once and it literally tasted like I was eating a bar of soap. I don't get the appeal. My grandma used to keep lavender soap in her guest bathroom, the kind shaped like little seashells that you weren't actually supposed to use. She had this whole nautical theme going on in there, with a lighthouse shower curtain and everything. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Stress? Yeah, I don't know. I guess I'm just normal when it comes to that.
Do you think your mind wanders or you get distracted in the same way when you're working on something you enjoy, like your dirt bike, as when you're doing other tasks?

Well, with the dirt bike, like I said, I'm totally locked in. But other stuff... yeah, it's way different. Actually, that's kind of what finally got me to come in here. Lately, I just can't keep my focus on one estimate or code form for work anymore. It's like, I'll sit down to do it, and then I hear a tool noise out in the shop, or I get a text, or I just get some new idea about how to redesign the workshop, and boom, I'm completely pulled off track. And then jobs start getting mixed up, which you really can't afford to do when you're an electrician. 

Speaking of the workshop, I was actually looking at getting this new heavy-duty pegboard system. The one I have now is just cheap particle board, and the pegs keep falling out every time I grab a wrench. My buddy was telling me about these magnetic tool strips you can mount directly to the studs instead. Magnets are crazy when you really think about it. Like, it's just this invisible force pulling metal together. We use magnetic fish tape at work sometimes to pull wire through blind walls, and it saves so much time. Time is money, right? Especially when the general contractor is breathing down your neck because the drywall guys are waiting. Man, drywall guys are always in such a rush, and they leave that fine white dust absolutely everywhere. I hate breathing that stuff in, it completely coats the inside of your nose and your throat. You'll be blowing your nose for days and it's just... 

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about the dirt bike again? Or work? I totally lost my train of thought.
Do you think you get more distracted when you're in a bad mood?

A bad mood? Um... I'm not really sure if it makes a difference, honestly. I don't get in bad moods all that often, unless I'm stuck in traffic. Traffic will definitely ruin my day. Especially on the interstate right now, they have that whole left lane closed down for miles and no one is even working on it. It's just endless rows of those bright orange barrels. 

I actually read somewhere that they use that specific shade of orange because it's the most visible color to the human eye in daylight. That's why hunting vests are that color, too. My uncle used to take me deer hunting upstate when I was a kid, and he made me wear this massive oversized orange vest that went down to my knees. It was freezing up there, though. We stayed in this tiny little cabin that only had a wood-burning stove for heat. Chopping wood is actually a great workout, you really feel it in your shoulders the next day. A lot of guys at the gym use those heavy battle ropes to get the same kind of burn, but I think chopping wood is way better because at least you're getting something useful done, you know? 

The gym just feels like a hamster wheel sometimes. You're just lifting heavy things to put them right back down in the exact same spot. Speaking of the gym, I really need to cancel my membership, they keep charging me an annual maintenance fee even though half the treadmills are broken. It's ridiculous. 

Wait, sorry. What was the question? Did you ask about the gym?
Do you think you get distracted as easily at home or when you're relaxing as you do at work?

At home? Um... I don't know, maybe? I guess when I'm relaxing, I don't really have to focus on much, so it doesn't matter if my mind wanders. I mostly just watch TV when I'm trying to relax, anyway. Lately I've been watching this whole series on deep sea exploration. It's wild what's down there. They found these hydrothermal vents where the water is boiling hot, but there are still all these weird crabs and tube worms living right next to them. 

Tube worms are crazy, they don't even have a mouth or a stomach. They just have these bacteria living inside them that turn the chemicals from the vents into food. It's called chemosynthesis, I think. It's kind of like photosynthesis, but without the sun. Which makes sense, because it's pitch black down there. I can't even imagine being in a submarine that deep. The pressure would just crush you instantly if there was a leak. That's why those submarines have to be built so thick, mostly out of titanium. Titanium is an incredible metal, they use it in airplanes and medical implants, too, because your body doesn't reject it. My dad actually had to get a titanium plate put in his collarbone after he wiped out on his motorcycle back in the nineties. He used to ride this massive Harley, it was loud as hell. You could hear him coming from three blocks away. Our neighbors hated it. The guy next door, Mr. Henderson, actually threatened to call the cops on him once because he was revving it up at six in the morning on a Sunday. Mr. Henderson was always complaining about something, though. His lawn was immaculate, like a golf course, and he'd get furious if any of our leaves blew over onto his grass. 

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about my dad? Or the TV? I lost track again.
Do you find your mind wandering or getting distracted when you're in a quiet room by yourself?

A quiet room? Um... well, yeah, actually. Even if it's quiet, it doesn't really help. Like I said before, that's kind of what finally got me to come in here. I'll be sitting by myself, trying to focus on one estimate or a code form for work, and it's just impossible anymore. Even if there's no noise, I'll just get some new idea about redesigning the workshop or something, and boom, I'm completely pulled off track. Or if I do hear just one little tool noise from the shop, or get a text, it's over. And then jobs start getting mixed up, which is a disaster. 

Speaking of the shop, I actually started looking into soundproofing it a little bit. You know, just to keep the noise from bleeding into the office area. They make this acoustic foam that looks like egg cartons, and you can just glue it right to the drywall. But I read that the foam doesn't actually block sound, it just stops it from echoing. If you really want to block sound, you have to use mass-loaded vinyl. It's this super heavy, dense rubber stuff on a roll. It's incredibly heavy, though. Like, you need two guys just to lift a roll of it. My buddy Steve helped me move a roll of it once, and he ended up tweaking his back. He had to go to a chiropractor for like three months after that. Chiropractors are wild, man. The way they crack your neck, it sounds like a dry branch snapping. It honestly kind of freaks me out. I feel like one wrong move and you're paralyzed, you know? But Steve swears by it. He says it's the only thing that helps his sciatica. Sciatica is no joke, it shoots right down your leg. 

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about Steve's back? Or the quiet room? I completely lost where I was going with that.
Do you think your distractibility is worse when you're feeling upset or angry?

Upset or angry? Um... I don't really know if it gets worse then. Honestly, I don't get super angry all that often. Well, unless I'm dealing with customer service on the phone. That will definitely get me going. Especially when you have to talk to that automated robot voice first, and it never understands what you're saying. You just keep yelling "representative" over and over again, and it's like, "I'm sorry, I didn't get that." It's infuriating. 

I heard they program those systems specifically to frustrate you so you'll just hang up and they don't have to pay a real person to talk to you. It's all about cutting costs. Just like how everything is made out of cheap plastic now instead of metal. Even tools. I bought this drill a few months ago, a brand name one, and the casing cracked the first time I dropped it from a ladder. Back in the day, tools were built to last forever. My grandpa had this old metal toolbox that weighed a ton, and the tools inside were practically indestructible. He had this one wrench that he used for everything. He even used it as a hammer sometimes, which you're really not supposed to do, but it worked. He was a mechanic, so he was always fixing something. His hands were permanently stained with grease, no matter how much he scrubbed them with that gritty orange soap. That stuff smells exactly like oranges, it's actually kind of nice. I think they use real citrus oil in it to cut through the grease. Citrus is actually a natural solvent. People use lemon juice to clean all kinds of things, like hard water stains on faucets. 

Wait, sorry... what were we just talking about? Did you ask about the drill? Or being angry? I got completely sidetracked again.
Do you think you're more easily distracted when you're feeling happy or excited?

Happy or excited? Um... yeah, I guess so. When I get really pumped up about something, my mind is just racing with all these ideas. Like, I'll get into this huge, elevated mood where I'm completely convinced our little shop is going to become the main solar outfit in the whole town. I'll be drawing up plans, talking a mile a minute about expanding and taking on commercial contracts. But the thing is, if my wife or one of the apprentices even slightly questions the plan, I just flip. I get so sharp with them over absolutely nothing, just because they aren't seeing the vision, you know? 

Solar is definitely the future, though. The efficiency on these new photovoltaic panels is insane compared to what they had even five years ago. They have these bifacial panels now that can absorb sunlight from both sides, so they catch the reflection off the roof or the ground. It boosts the output by like twenty percent. You just have to make sure you mount them at the exact right angle, depending on your latitude, to get the maximum sun exposure year-round. A lot of people don't realize you have to factor in the tilt of the earth during winter versus summer. It's all trigonometry, really. I always hated math in high school, but now I use it every day. My geometry teacher, Mr. Gable, always said we'd use it in the real world, and we all just laughed at him. He was this quirky guy who always wore these loud, patterned bow ties. Every single day, a different bow tie. He said he had a collection of over two hundred of them. I think he used to buy them at vintage shops or estate sales. Estate sales are actually pretty cool, you can find some amazing old tools and furniture for dirt cheap. People just want to clear out the house, so they practically give stuff away. 

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about the solar panels? Or being excited? I completely lost the thread again.
Do you think your distractibility gets better or worse when you're in a calm and relaxed state?

Calm and relaxed? Um... man, I don't even know if I ever really get to that state anymore. But honestly, even if I try to just sit still and be calm, it doesn't fix it. Like I was saying earlier, that's what finally pushed me to come in here. I'll be sitting down, trying to just calmly look over one single estimate or a code form for work, and I just can't keep my focus on it. It's like my brain won't let me stay on task. If I hear one tool noise from the guys in the shop, or my phone buzzes with a text, or even if I just get some random new idea about reorganizing the workshop, I'm completely pulled off track. And then jobs start getting mixed up, which is just a total disaster for the business. 

Speaking of the business, we actually had to switch our accounting software last month because the old one kept crashing. It was this ancient program that looked like it was built in the nineties. The new one is all cloud-based, which is supposed to be better, but the interface is super confusing. It's got all these colorful graphs and dashboards that just feel like overkill. My buddy Dave uses the same software for his landscaping company, and he said it took him weeks to figure it out. Landscaping is a tough gig, man. Being out in the sun all day, dealing with all those bugs. Dave got bit by a tick last summer and had to go on antibiotics for a month because they thought he might have Lyme disease. Lyme disease is scary stuff, it can mess up your joints for life if you don't catch it early. They say you're supposed to wear long pants when you're in the woods, but who wants to do that when it's ninety degrees out? 

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about Dave's landscaping? Or the code forms? I totally lost track of what I was answering.
Do you think your distractibility is worse when you're feeling overwhelmed?

Overwhelmed? Um... I don't know. I mean, maybe? I guess I don't really notice if it's worse when I'm overwhelmed because I'm just always kind of scattered lately. But man, being overwhelmed is just part of the job, you know? Especially when we get a huge shipment of supplies in all at once. Like last Tuesday, this massive delivery of conduit and wiring came in, and the driver backed his truck right into the neighbor's fence. Just smashed right through it. The neighbor is this older guy, Mr. Henderson, and he was furious. He came storming out in his bathrobe, yelling about his prize-winning roses that got crushed. He grows these huge, bright red roses, I think they're called Chrysler Imperials or something. My mom used to grow roses when I was a kid. She had this whole garden in the backyard, and she spent hours out there pruning them and spraying them with this weird-smelling bug stuff. She always wore these thick leather gloves so she wouldn't get pricked by the thorns. Thorns are actually an evolutionary defense mechanism for plants, to keep animals from eating them. It's crazy how nature adapts like that. Like how some frogs in the rainforest are brightly colored to warn predators that they're poisonous. I saw a documentary about that once. The frogs secrete this toxin through their skin, and the indigenous tribes used to rub their blowdarts on the frogs before hunting. 

Wait... sorry, what did you ask me? Was it about the fence? Or being overwhelmed? My mind just totally drifted off again.
Do you think your distractibility is worse when you're feeling anxious or under a lot of pressure?

Anxious or under pressure? I mean, yeah, pressure definitely doesn't help. Like I was telling you a minute ago, that's exactly why I'm sitting here. I'll be under the gun to finish an estimate or fill out a code form for an inspection, and I just can't keep my eyes on the paper. One guy drops a wrench in the shop, or my phone dings, or I suddenly think we need to build new shelving for the copper wire, and boom, I'm doing that instead. Then the jobs get all mixed up. And in my line of work, mixing things up under pressure is bad news. You're dealing with live wires. One wrong move and you get a serious shock. You have to wear these super thick rubber-soled boots. They weigh a ton. 

It's crazy to think rubber actually comes from trees, you know? They tap the trees to get the sap, kind of like how they make maple syrup up in Vermont. I took a trip to Vermont once with my ex-girlfriend. We went in the fall to see the leaves change. The colors were unbelievable, just bright oranges and reds everywhere. We stayed in this little bed and breakfast that smelled like cinnamon and old wood. The owner made us these huge stacks of pancakes every morning with real, local syrup. Not that fake corn syrup stuff you buy at the grocery store. High fructose corn syrup is literally in everything now. I was reading the back of a ketchup bottle the other day, and it was the second ingredient. Ketchup shouldn't be sweet, it's supposed to be savory. Tomatoes are technically a fruit, though, which I always found weird. Like, who puts fruit on a hamburger? 

Wait, sorry... did you ask about the boots? Or being anxious? I totally lost what I was talking about.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others or blurting out answers before they finish speaking?

Interrupting people? Um... I don't know, maybe? I don't really notice if I do. I mean, my guys at the shop haven't said anything about it. But then again, they're mostly focused on getting their hours in and getting out. We've got this one apprentice, Tommy, who never stops talking anyway. He's always going on about his dirt bike. He bought this used Yamaha last month and he's been trying to rebuild the engine himself. I keep telling him he needs to make sure the carburetor is clean before he tries to run it, but he won't listen. Carburetors are tricky, man. If you get even a little speck of dirt in the jet, the whole thing runs lean and you can burn up a piston. My dad used to rebuild old muscle cars when I was growing up, so I learned a lot about engines from him. He had this beautiful '69 Chevelle SS. Midnight blue with white racing stripes. We used to take it to car shows on the weekends. The guys at the shows were always so intense, polishing their chrome until you could see your reflection in it. Chrome plating is actually a really toxic process, they use hexavalent chromium, which is that stuff from the Erin Brockovich movie. Julia Roberts was so good in that. I haven't seen a movie in a theater in forever. The popcorn is always way too salty now, and a soda costs like eight bucks. 

Wait... what did you ask me? Was it about Tommy? Or the shop? I totally lost my train of thought again.
Do you think your distractibility changes when you're feeling sad or down?

Sad or down? Um, I don't really know if it's different then. Like I was saying before, it's just bad all the time right now. That's what finally got me in here, honestly. I just can't keep my focus on one estimate or code form anymore. It's like, I'll be sitting there trying to calculate the load for a new subpanel, and then I hear a tool drop in the shop, or I get a text, or I suddenly get this great idea about how we need to reorganize the workshop, and I'm just gone. I get pulled totally off track. And then jobs start getting mixed up, which is a huge problem. 

Speaking of mixing things up, I actually accidentally grabbed the wrong gauge wire for a job last week. I was supposed to grab 12-gauge for some outlets, but I grabbed 14-gauge instead. Luckily I caught it before we ran it, because 14-gauge is only rated for 15 amps, and if you put it on a 20-amp breaker, the wire can overheat before the breaker trips. That's how fires start. House fires are terrifying. I saw this news story about a family who lost everything because of a faulty space heater. Space heaters pull so much power. People just plug them into these cheap extension cords that aren't rated for that kind of wattage, and the cord just melts. Plastic melting smells so bad. It's like burning tires. I drove past a tire fire once when I was a kid. The smoke was this thick, black cloud that you could see for miles. It took them days to put it out because tires are basically just solid fuel. They use petroleum to make synthetic rubber, which is why they burn so hot. Petroleum is in everything, man. Even Vaseline is petroleum jelly. I used to put Vaseline on my chapped lips in the winter, but then I read somewhere that you're basically just putting crude oil on your mouth. 

Wait, sorry... what were you asking me? Was it about the space heaters? Or being sad? I lost my train of thought again.
Do you think your distractibility is worse when you're feeling happy or excited?

Happy or excited? Yeah, I guess so. Actually, when I'm feeling really good, like really pumped up, that's when things get kind of intense. Like, I'll get this huge burst of energy and I'll start talking about how our little shop is going to become the main solar outfit in the whole town. Solar is the future, you know? The tax credits they're giving out right now are insane. My buddy Dave put panels on his roof last year and his electric bill is literally zero now. He even sells power back to the grid. The grid in this country is so outdated, though. It's crazy how vulnerable the whole system is. I watched this documentary about how a massive solar flare could knock out the entire power grid for months. It happened back in the 1800s, the Carrington Event, they called it. Telegraph wires were literally sparking and catching fire. Imagine if that happened today, with everything running on computers. People would lose their minds. Without the internet, nobody knows how to do anything anymore. I tried to use a paper map the other day when my phone died, and it was a nightmare trying to fold it back up. My dad always kept a Rand McNally atlas in the glovebox of his truck. He knew every backroad in the county. 

But anyway, yeah, when I'm in that pumped-up mood talking about the solar expansion, if my wife or one of the apprentices even questions the plan, I can just flip. I get super sharp with them over absolutely nothing. It's like I have zero patience. 

Wait, did you ask about solar panels? Or the shop? I totally lost track of what we were talking about again.
Do you think your distractibility changes when you're feeling emotionally neutral, compared to when you're feeling happy, sad, or anxious?

Emotionally neutral? Um... I don't really know what that feels like right now, honestly. It's hard to tell if the distractibility is different because I don't think I've been neutral in a long time. I'm either totally dragging or I'm wired. But I guess if I think back to when things were normal... I don't know, it's a blur. It's like trying to remember what a room looked like before you painted it. We painted our living room this color called "Navajo White" last year, which is really just a fancy name for beige. It took three coats because the walls were previously this awful mustard yellow. Yellow is such a hard color to paint over. You have to use a really good primer, like Kilz. Kilz is amazing stuff, it covers up anything. I used it once to cover up some water stains on a ceiling after a pipe burst in this old Victorian house we were rewiring. Victorian houses are a nightmare for electricians, man. They have this old knob-and-tube wiring that is just a fire hazard waiting to happen. The insulation on the wires just crumbles into dust when you touch it. Dust is mostly just dead skin cells, which is super gross if you think about it. I read that a typical mattress doubles in weight over ten years just from accumulated dust mites and skin. That's why you're supposed to vacuum your mattress. My wife bought this special vacuum attachment just for the bed, it has this UV light on it that's supposed to kill the mites. UV light is basically just radiation. That's why you get sunburns. I got a terrible sunburn once when we went fishing down in the Keys. We were out on the boat all day and I forgot to reapply sunscreen. 

Wait... what was the question? Were you asking about the house? Or the boat? I completely forgot what we were talking about.
Has your difficulty with focusing and getting distracted always been a part of your life, or is this something that you've noticed changing over time?

No, it definitely hasn't always been this bad. It's something that's really been changing and building up over time... I'd say for about seven months now? Yeah, it started right around the time we took on the mortgage for the new workshop and bought all the upgraded equipment. 

Mortgages are just insane right now, by the way. The interest rates are absolutely brutal. We had to go through this local credit union because the big commercial banks wouldn't even look at us without a massive down payment. Banks are such a scam anyway, honestly. They just take your money, lend it out to other people at high rates, and then give you like, what, a fraction of a percent on your savings? It's literally pennies. I actually used to collect pennies when I was a kid. My grandpa got me one of those blue cardboard coin folders—you know the ones where you press the coins into the little slots? I was obsessed with finding a 1943 steel penny. They had to make them out of steel during World War II because they needed all the copper for the war effort, like for wiring and ammunition. Ammunition is so incredibly expensive now, too. I went to the shooting range with my buddy a few weeks ago and a box of standard 9mm was just... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Did you ask about the mortgage? I totally lost my train of thought again.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, or have trouble staying seated when you need to?

Staying seated? Yeah, sitting still just feels like a massive waste of time right now. I’ve honestly been going nonstop. Like, bouncing from job sites to doing bids, and then I'm back at the workshop rewiring test panels. I keep starting all these new home-automation ideas before the last one is even done, just because I have to be moving and doing something. 

Speaking of home automation, it's getting kind of creepy, honestly. I was hooking up this smart hub for a client last week, and those things are definitely listening to you. My wife and I were just talking about buying a new coffee maker—not even searching for it on our phones, just talking out loud in the kitchen—and the next day, boom, ads for espresso machines everywhere on my feed. Espresso is way too bitter for me, anyway. I don't get how people drink it straight. My old boss used to drink three shots of espresso before 8 AM. He was this huge guy, ex-Navy, used to tell us these crazy stories about being stationed on a submarine. Can you imagine being trapped in a metal tube underwater for months? The water pressure down there is insane. If there's even a tiny leak, the water shoots in so fast it cuts through steel like a laser. Lasers are actually super interesting, they use them for everything now, even eye surgery. My aunt got LASIK last year and she said she could literally smell her own eyeball burning during the procedure. Which is just... so gross. I could never do that. I hate anything touching my eyes. 

Wait... why was I talking about LASIK? Did you ask about my eyesight? Or the smart hubs? I completely lost the thread again, sorry. What was the question?
